notes.title: Patch 1.0.3.7805 is live now!
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings fellow Nubs,[/h1][p][/p][p]A new update has been launched by order of the great Konzumos![/p][p][/p][p]In this update we have performed some significant updates to the local play and controller input handling. 
Players will now have full control over what controller is assigned to what user/player, have different bindings saved for different controller hardware types, and can set up local play with keyboard and mouse + controller hybrid play.[/p][p][/p][p]A full overview of the changes can be found below:
[/p][h3]LOCAL PLAY[/h3][list][*][p]Local player UI will now show all the correct information for the correct local players in their designated UI locations.[/p][/*][*][p]Local player naming, numbering and sorting will no longer get (potentially) scrambled when playing with more than 2 players.[/p][/*][*][p]Passive selection will now show the player name for all players.[/p][/*][*][p]Changed the local player names to Player 1,2,3,4 instead of the primary player username. This fixes some clarity issues when dealing with long user names.[/p][/*][*][p]When a local player is removed from the game during the player selection screen, the remaining local player names and indices will be shifted so that there are no gaps in the player name numberings. When a slot gap is refilled by a player, the naming and numbering will shift again accordingly. This improves clarity and consistency based on the number of active players during the local match.[/p][/*][*][p]When playing in local play, each player will now have input icons that match their controller hardware type. General UI such as menus will follow the input device of the primary player/user.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]INPUT[/h3][list][*][p]Controller rebinding will now be aborted when a controller is connected and/or disconnected during the binding process.[/p][/*][*][p]Drastically improved the controller handling and customization within the game.[/p][list][*][p]You can now select and adjust the individual attached controllers in the controller settings menu. The selected controller will provide a slight rumble to confirm the current selection if the controller is recognized and supported. Each recognized controller type can be modified and have it's bindings adjusted. Saved changes are shared per controller hardware type for all players/users.[/p][/*][*][p]The controller binding menu will now show what controller you are changing as well as the user and/or player that the target controller is assigned to.[/p][/*][*][p]Controller assignment can now be adjusted from the settings menu (both in the main, pause menu and player join screen) on the fly. A quick access option has also been made available in the player join screen. This gives the user full control over what controller device is assigned to which user and/or player.[/p][/*][*][p]For people with disabilities, this also allows you to assign multiple controllers to the same player if needed.[/p][/*][*][p]For people who would like to play with player 1 on a keyboard and player 2 on a single controller, this can now also be easily configured.[/p][/*][*][p]Supports manual configuration, auto configuration and input polling controller assignment.[/p][/*][*][p]Resetting of the bindings can now be done per controller hardware type instead of auto resetting this for all hardware types.[/p][/*][*][p]Unrecognized and native unsupported controllers will now be highlighted so that you can know if your connected controller will function or not without having Steam Input enabled.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]The input binding save data structure has been adjusted to improve the save data formatting. Existing bindings will be auto upgraded and converted.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where controller binding adjustments would clear the bindings for the other attached controllers of the same hardware type until the game was restarted.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue when players want to play the game locally with a mix of controllers and keyboard that causes the UI to constantly alter between keyboard and mouse icons and controller icons.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where players would aim towards the mouse target when playing with a hybrid of keyboard and mouse and controller in local play.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]UI[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where certain popups could remain active in the input binding menu when you would start a match while matchmaking during input rebinding.[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Nublog #13 | The First Post Launch Blog!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/680449a0066718d9fe563e0ca8377bca0600c3eb.png[/img]

Hey everyone, we're back again with another Nublog! 

First off, we want to give a huge thank you to all of you who have jumped into Nubs! Arena since our launch. Your enthusiasm and feedback have been invaluable to us and we had so much fun seeing everyone jump into the game and enjoy it with their friends!

We also want to take this time to acknowledge that some players have encountered technical issues, including, matchmaking difficulties, performance hiccups and local play issues. We want you to know that we are actively working to address these problems and are committed to improving the game's stability and performance. We really appreciate your patience, stick with us!

Our team is dedicated to making Nubs! Arena the best experience it can be. Your feedback is crucial in helping us identify and fix issues. Please continue to share your experiences with us on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2337860/]Steam Community Hub[/url] and [url=https://discord.com/invite/nubs]Discord[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/35c16a1bfaacb4c07c81ab06ea32960058521378.png[/img]

RADAR Festival is a three-day event where fans of boundary-pushing music come together to experience live performances from a wide range of progressive artists, from heavy technical bands to genre-blending experimental acts. Alongside the music, the festival offers masterclasses, a music industry market, and a welcoming atmosphere that encourages connection between artists, fans, and industry professionals.

And you too could go! Because we are giving 2 tickets away for the festival [url=https://x.com/FollowNubs/status/1930565671915544792]over on our Twitter![/url] So leave a comment there and with a bit of luck the ticket will be yours!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/508f9db4d905fce229e4b88303727a832044fc35.png[/img]

Thanks again for jumping in, having fun, reporting bugs, and being part of this weird little party brawler. More updates are coming soon, stay tuned!

– Glowfish and Rangatang

notes.title: Patch 1.0.2.7712 is live now!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello,[/h1]

Nubs! dev team here. We've got another patch for you! This one focuses on resolving additional connectivity issues and introducing quality settings to improve performance, particularly for players on low-end devices.
We've also gathered feedback and made several small adjustments to improve overall gameplay.

[h3]GENERAL
[/h3]- Fixed a rare game client crash.
- Fixed a jitter issue that occurred under specific conditions.
- Fixed an issue where player names would not appear if the network connection had high packet loss.
- Fixed a memory leak in the character renderer.
- Improved lag compensation for unstable connections.
- Improved performance in the Score Screen (the little room where players wait for the next round to start).
- Added an alternative method for determining ping to help with optimal server selection for players who are unable to perform standard ping requests.

[h3]QUALITY SETTINGS[/h3]
- Added Dynamic Resolution setting:
Disabled: Don't use the dynamic resolution and render at your configured resolution.
Auto: Automatically scale the resolution between the configured resolution and the provided resolution scale to try and reach the target FPS. (Respects the target FPS setting if enabled, otherwise defaults to 60 fps as the target).
Fixed: Full control over the resolution scaling which will be fixed to the provided resolution scale.
- Added Character Rendering Resolution: Allows player characters to be rendered at a lower resolution to improve performance, at the cost of visual fidelity.
- Adjusted default quality and display settings for Steam Deck users. Existing players on Steam Deck will keep their current settings but can reset the display and quality settings in the settings menu to match the new Steamdeck defaults. (strongly recommended!)

[h3]GENERAL GAMEPLAY[/h3]
- Fire Damage: Damage per tick reduced from 4 to 2. Total fire damage reduced from 20 to 10.
- Star Shards: Slightly increased chance of finding star shards from chests or bushes, making it more feasible to collect 5 in a round (instead of often being stuck at 4).
- Melee Powerup: Improved rotation responsiveness while under the effects of the melee powerup.
- Level Selection: Now takes player count into account—smaller maps are excluded at higher player counts.

[h3]ITEMS[/h3]
- Boomer-ang: Increased movement speed by 25%. Damage per hit increased from 16 to 18.
- Linger-Spinner: Now remains in place upon collision for the duration of its effect, instead of bouncing back immediately. This should make it more reliable and controllable.
- Invulnerabili-Tea: Now displays "Immune" when attacking a player under its effect to clarify that all damage is being blocked.

[h3]PASSIVES[/h3]
- Extra-Goodies: Rather than dropping an extra set of Goodies, this passive now gives the player +1 extra charge when picking up any Goody.
We noticed this passive wasn't having much impact on a player's ability to win and often benefited opponents, as players couldn’t always use all the extra loot dropped. By increasing charges instead of spawning more Goodies, this passive should now be significantly more useful.

[h3]UI
[/h3]- Fixed an issue where selection could be lost in the pause menu when using a controller.
- Fixed an issue where players could partially cancel passive selection by pressing the cancel button or opening the pause menu during the selection process.
- The splash screen now maintains proper aspect ratios and will no longer stretch.
- Added a game introduction sequence shown on first launch.
(Existing players will also see this one-time welcome, which includes useful gameplay info. This overview is also accessible via the main and pause menus.)
- Input fields now behave more reliably with controller input and fully support Steam Deck and Steam Big Picture Mode.
- Fixed a selection issue when switching between mouse and joystick input in the tabbed UI.
- Added UI scale retargeting for lower aspect ratios to ensure optimal UI display on those aspect ratios.
- Added additional safeguards to prevent certain settings menus from appearing blank or getting stuck.
- Fixed an issue where the GameInfo display at the top left would overlap other elements. Its background is now semi-transparent to reduce screen clutter.
- Fixed a white arrow artifact seen on players at the map edge when using ultrawide monitors.
- The pause menu now closes correctly when entering the victory screen, preventing UI conflicts and confusion.

[h3]LOCALIZATION[/h3]
- Added Japanese version of the game logo.
- Fixed Russian font settings to correct rendering and text color issues.

[h3]ACHIEVEMENTS
[/h3]- Fixed an issue where match wins weren’t always tracked for the “Bestest” achievement. Wins earned during the bugged period should now be retroactively counted—no wins lost!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.1.7522 is live now!
notes.content:
Hello,

Nubs! dev team here. We appreciate everyone playing (and hopefully enjoying:)) the game. A special thank you to everyone reporting issues! Anyone experiences any issues can contact us on [url=https://discord.gg/nubs]Discord[/url] or the Steam community page.

We have a first patch (1.0.1.7522) ready:

[b]CRASHES[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed a rare crash when there are lots of status effects going on.
[*] Fixed a rare server crash when a player leaves during a match.
[/list]

[b]CONNECTION[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed endless "Finding best Regions" for some users with a poor connection to our servers. If you still experience this issue after the update, please add the game to the whitelist of your anti-virus software and firewall.
[/list]

[b]UI[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where controller input would be locked when selected a character that cannot customise certain settings.
[*] Fixed an issue where the skins in the character customisation would still be visible outside of the selection box for a single frame when using controller input.
[*] The redeem code result message will now be cleared when clearing the input field and when re-entering the redeem code screen.
[*] Fixed an issue where when you would redeem a code or unlock a new item while in one of the menus after opening the customization menu, the unlocked item lists would not correctly resort to show the available items on top,
[*] Fixed an issue where the passive selection screen would keep scaling down with each player in local play and with a non-default UI scale active
[*] Fixed a potential error with the interactable messaging prompt while the interactable is destroyed or picked up by someone else
[/list]

[b]DLC[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue which caused 2 emotes of the Nubs! Emote Pack DLC to not unlock. All people who have purchased this should now correctly have those 2 emotes.
[/list]

[b]!COMING SOON![/b]
[list]
[*] We are aware some players are having performance issues. We are hard at work to resolve these issues and expect an update on that front soon.
[*] Extra connection/latencies improvements
[*] Fixes to controller issues in local play mode
[/list]

- Glowfish and Rangatang

notes.title: Nubs! Arena is Out Now!
notes.content:
[h3]The arena gates have officially BURST OPEN – Nubs! Arena is now LIVE on Steam!
[/h3]

[previewyoutube=bCsUuBaMdQo;full][/previewyoutube]

After months of fixing bugs, testing chaotic builds, and wrestling with physics so dumb they loop back to genius, it's finally time for you to join the Arena. The fight begins NOW!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/9b5535ecd4a6298c83db415ed1827eb428ff3ccb.png[/img]

For those just jumping in, Nubs! is an over-the-top PvP arena brawler inspired by the charm (and chaos) of classic top-down RPGs. Take control of your Nub and fight your way through deadly arenas with bizarre traps. Snag ridiculous weapons, unleash absurd power-ups, and win the crowd to earn the favor of the all-powerful Konzumos!

Here’s what you’ll be doing in Nubs!:


[list]
[*] [b]Create the perfect Nub for you[/b] – Customize your Nub with an outrageous mix of outfits and colors to stand out.
[*] [b]Survive Deadly Arenas[/b] – Fight in a range of colorful and dangerous stages, each filled with unique hazards and surprise elements.
[*] [b]Wield the Ridiculous[/b] – Arm yourself with a bizarre arsenal of weapons and power-ups, ranging from powerful to just plain weird (including fish).
[*] [b]Mix Up Your Matches[/b] – Jump into free-for-alls, team battles, and soon to come additional game modes.
[*] [b]Multiplayer Madness[/b] – Play online or locally with up to 20 players in total mayhem.
[*] [b]Fast and Addictive[/b] – What starts as one quick match often turns into an all-night brawl.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/66a0345b2654002f22bd67df5db1db77a3bc8091.png[/img]

Joins us in Nubs the first week and get the Royal Nub skin for free. This way you can show off to everyone that you were there day one!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/LxRExTT.gif[/img]

And here’s more! The following days after launch we and many content creators will be sharing keys for free skins on [url=https://x.com/FollowNubs]our X[/url], so make sure you’re following us there to not miss them!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/VlnDydC.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/1edcb3d3a375b0c084b6146e32da48c9233d3316.png[/img]

AND THERE'S EVEN MORE! The coming months after release we will drop new weapons, new maps, enemies, passives, rewards and seasonal items. All for free! 

You can see the Roadmap for Nubs: Arena here: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/6200800ec3fc4b5b1afd660387360069026ea63a.png[/img] 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/c0ca3929edadfd0be3c3d23b001b70cb5557857e.png[/img]

Invite a friend (or 20), blow each other up! And remember that, yes, lava hurts. Drop a review if you're loving the chaos, and tag us in your best arena moments on [url=https://x.com/FollowNubs]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/@PlayNubs]YouTube[/url] and [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@nubs_game]TikTok[/url] we want to see how wild it gets out there. 

See you in the arena,
- Glowfish and Rangatang

notes.title: Former Awesomenauts developers finish the game they were working on when the studio went bankrupt in 2023, and it'll be free for the first 24 hours after release
notes.content: wesomenauts developer Ronimo Games filed for bankruptcy in 2023, bringing a premature end to an unnamed project it had in development. But a year later, four former members of the studio including the CEO got back together to form a new studio called Rangatang and resumed work on the project, which is now set to launch on May 15—and if you grab it within the first 24 hours of release, it's yours to keep forever... Read more.

notes.title: Nublog #10 | The Road to Nubs!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/d7c8dfa1463aecaa7cc80d654e15fdc18c1d5ddf.png[/img]

Hey, you Nub!

This week, we’re diving into the origins of Nubs!, how the game came to life, the inspiration behind its chaotic fun, and the journey of how a simple dungeon crawler was molded into a full-fledged multiplayer arena game.

So sit back, grab your favorite snack, we've got a story to tell.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/6260bc9fdefbe4c57e059400a9c81de7bca4d588.png[/img]

Once upon a time in the Netherlands, a passionate gaming studio known as Ronimo Games carved a niche for themselves in the gaming world. Their creations, notably Awesomenauts and Blightbound, were celebrated for their accessibility and competitive depth, captivating players worldwide. This success fueled their ambition, leading them to conceptualize a new project, a whimsical, Zelda-esque dungeon crawler with a multiplayer twist, featuring quirky characters embarking on grand adventures, wielding unconventional weapons to vanquish formidable bosses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/944d7d67269b070445e5283da7a0af6da9615d71.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/66b4fefc756951d6101e3b5ea036182bf2506b37.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/e3adbbbaab7e68e32eedcbe2fa02a1fb36508153.png[/img]

However, as the project progressed, unforeseen challenges began to surface. Plans shifted, obstacles mounted, and circumstances beyond the team's control created an uphill battle. In the end, the development of the Zelda-esque game came to an abrupt and unfortunate halt, leaving its future uncertain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/f8464a0ef433cacbc4c15322f4c4d7ecb66c220c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/92203f355633fdc7696408abec159f25e86b47b5.png[/img]

Yet, from this adversity, a new hope emerged. Four former members of Ronimo were determined to create something simple and fun and to do justice to the great work done by Ronimo. These were  Maarten ( Ronimo's Lead Programmer), Machiel (Ronimo's Core Tech Programmer), Olivier (Ronimo's CEO), and Gijs (Ronimo's Concept Artist).

When they played the game with Belgian developer Glowfish Interactive, they hit it off so well that they decided to join powers and together create the game you now know as Nubs!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/0d81587db9679408dbab4793b47ebd8793abfddb.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/a5b76ba21e33a883d566dc11dbd007f569faa37f.png[/img]

This partnership breathed new life into the project, giving the team the opportunity to not only refine upon their original vision but also to salvage and repurpose a vast number of assets from their previous work. Instead of starting from scratch, they reworked existing designs, environments, and mechanics, ensuring that the heart of their original game lived on in Nubs!. With renewed determination, they pressed forward, transforming setbacks into opportunities and crafting an experience that hopefully everyone will enjoy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/12ed71f3f218bd1b2b5da3541c02a27d6655bd9b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/ecb78c9b17c944e66ef1c69135484585cf022380.png[/img]

That's everything you need to know! Keep your eyes peeled on our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2337860/Nubs_Arena/]Steam[/url] and [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/nubs/]Reddit[/url] because in less than 2 weeks we'll talk about something very exciting.

Speak to you soon,
-Rangatang and Glowfish

notes.title: Nublog #7 | Your Feedback Is Improving Nubs!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/dc763cdf20516e9d6ae6fc098e0ffdd38f5790e6.png[/img]

After the Nubs! playtest last month, we've been hard at work gathering and reviewing all the feedback we've received from you. Your input has been incredibly valuable and has given us so much insight into what’s working well and what could be improved. 

We’ve been carefully going through every comment, suggestion, and piece of advice to ensure we’re making the game the best it can be. Your feedback is helping shape the future of Nubs! so we wanted to share some of the changes we made thanks to your feedback!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/0387abb76d1d19864fad7fb266fa181b6cf23cd8.png[/img]

We've noticed that many players have been struggling to identify the upcoming/current game mode. To help this, we've added a bright, colorful loading bar and a banner at the start of each match. We hope this makes it easier for players to understand the next objective and limits confusion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/1aef1a03da69e3617c34ac285241eae55aa069d5.gif[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/8yjxr63.gif[/img]

A lot of players also felt as though melee combat was a bit too 'spammy' and not as satisfying. To fix this we've upped the cool-down between each swing. We think this will help swords feel more skill based and fun to fight with.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/b6FRGzI.gif[/img]

We’ve received feedback from many players that they often didn’t notice when they were hitting teammates instead of opponents. To make this more obvious, we’ve added text bubbles to help clear up any confusion during gameplay.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/OsBbIDh.gif[/img]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/416f705f481d4e4eb60825a2deec28be509db102.png[/img]

Those were some of the changes we made since the last playtest. Still missing some changes? Don't worry! There's still a lot of additions and adjustments that we did not cover in this Nublog. 

This playtest also certainly was not the last! So to see all the changes we made thanks to you, you can join our next playtest. Follow our [url=https://x.com/FollowNubs]Twitter [/url]or [url=https://bsky.app/profile/playnubs.bsky.social]Bluesky [/url]to get notified on when the next one will be.

That’s a wrap on this week's Nublog. Stay tuned for the next Nublog, because more info on future playtests will be shared soon! Get ready to unleash your inner Nub!

Speak to you soon,
-Rangatang and Glowfish

notes.title: Nublog #2 | What have we been up to!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/ce2272e1f25574d42783f865823dfac46ae63189.png[/img]

Welcome back Nubs, happy to have you again! In today's Nublog we have some interesting behind the scenes on some of the stuff we've been working on the past few weeks. Check it out! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/d4d36e18f2819d081cf6093da3211117065be3c1.png[/img]

One of the many important parts of game development is creating instant feedback. Whatever a player is doing, having visual or sound cues that acknowledges players' actions is extremely important, and often overlooked in many games. 

For a chaotic game like Nubs it is important for those visual cues to not fall flat. Exaggerating animations is something that helps with this a lot! 

For instance, when hitting an exploding barrel, it will immediately start spewing fire! This is super-over-the-top but it catches the eye and makes sure the player feels as though they really hit it!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/8e9603762b3f66d5626f5b4a1c54a07f24d7c4d3.gif[/img]



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/b4db7ea4b44fa2d181999179f1a48129ff1d1646.png[/img]


Originally, we used a grid-based system to place all water, terrain, and walls in the game. Artists then had to paint each corner or edge in Photoshop and set up rules for when and where those tiles would appear. 

This approach made the world easy to design and kept gameplay consistent. But when it came to natural features, like small ponds, the rigid grid made things look unnatural.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/4af272cf142d235e0c349a32e19ee80bbb400986.png[/img]

For creating little ponds of water we needed something more free-flowing. A system that allows us to weave water around big rocks and is flexible to allow smooth shallow transitions with less work for artists. 

So now we use a combination of splines and custom-made shaders/materials to achieve a look that we're happy with. It allows us to change the parameters defining the foaming, colors, and transition/interaction with the underlying surface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/aa8b32fec732b5c8357371ac4f71b0d47b488489.png[/img]
Notice that we now have multiple layers in the water body, allowing us to submerge pebbles & rocks and easily change the border. It results in a flexible, reusable system that's a joy to work with.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/af2cc78f71cc8e731fd8931c2d43e52df54a9e03.png[/img]


The chaos is what makes Nubs! fun! To create more of it, we wanted to add "fake" physics to all interactions. This makes the game feel more alive, responsive and in a way, make more sense. 

To achieve this a lot of simple interactions get added to objects to create more unpredictable behavior. These elements include: 
[list]
[*] Adding a delay to explosive objects so they can be knocked around instead of exploding right away
[*] Adding knockback to all damage, even the smallest things, like arrows, ensuring that everything receives knockback. Even elements you would not expect at first like dropped weapons on the ground.
[*] some "fake" physics pass along knockback from one object to the other.
[/list]

Here are the results!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/210f99e0b10c49cbb7edc66a1b3f578faa7d1202.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/cf2155f2bc85c0cfab44a30247c3a72aa77470b9.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/62bafbe19e3fb0ee9b406623cc8eb39215027579.png[/img]

That’s a wrap on this week's Nublog. Stay tuned for future Nublogs, because more development updates will be shared with you every two weeks. Get ready to unleash your inner Nub!
-Greetings, Nublognub

notes.title: Nublog #1 | Meet The Devs!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/f728b999ecf3d16b413daed1b7e8f4cf95485812.png[/img]Known for titles like Awesomenauts, Space Pirate Trainer, Trifox, and Blightbound. These teams don’t lack experience nor skill! In this very first [b]Nublog[/b] we’ll take a closer look at the creative minds from Rangatang and Glowfish that are shaping the world of Nubs!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/3a63ae0e54214b47550dc0f8e87f242d0f3808b1.png[/img][b]Olivier Thijssen 
[/b]
Olivier has been around the block (and then some) with 16 years of experience as Co-Founder, Artist, Designer, Creative Director, and CEO at Ronimo Games. He’s got some serious street cred, with titles like the indie MOBA hit Awesomenauts under his belt. But Olivier isn’t just a title-collector, he’s got the chops in everything from game design to art, project scoping, business wrangling, and even making sure the cash flow doesn’t run dry! His mix of big-picture thinking and hands-on know-how is part of what’s making Nubs! as ridiculous and fun as it is.

[b]Gijs Witkamp 
[/b]
Gijs has been whipping up awesome 2D art for about 5 years at Ronimo Games (with 1.5 years of internships thrown in for good measure). He’s got an honors degree in Creative Media from the Utrecht School of the Arts, so yeah, he knows his stuff when it comes to game art. Gijs played a huge role in shaping the style of Blightbound and Ronimo’s latest project, and he’s lent his skills to plenty of in-house pitches, including Awesomenauts. Whether it’s graphic design, animation, illustration, or concept art, Gijs can do it all, making sure Nubs! looks as fun as it plays!
 
[b]Machiel van Hooren 
[/b]
Machiel’s been deep in the gaming world for about 13 years, coding up all sorts of wild stuff. His last gig was at Ronimo Games as Core Tech Lead. Along with Maarten and Olivier, he co-founded Rangatang to keep the fun going. Machiel’s a programming wizard, handling everything from gameplay and game engine development to porting, networking, and even compiler development (don’t worry I also don’t know what that means). So when it comes to making Nubs! run smoothly, he’s got it covered!
 
[b]Maarten van den Heijkant 
[/b]
Maarten spent over 13 years at Ronimo Games, helping bring all their games to life. As a programmer, he’s got tons of experience in gameplay, networking, matchmaking, and making sure everything runs smoothly with performance optimization. Basically, if it involves getting the game to play just right, Maarten’s the guy making it happen. Now, he’s bringing that same expertise to Nubs! to make sure every match is as fast, fun, and chaotic as possible!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/fd8222093eeb4e830ab8346f60ce29b82c7da894.png[/img]
[b]Brecht Lecluyse
[/b]
Brecht has been in the game dev scene for over 20 years, starting out as a hobbyist before going pro in 2009. As a game development jack-of-all-trades, he’s got hands-on experience with every part of the game-making process and is all about delivering top-notch quality on every front. Now, he's bringing that expertise to Nubs! to make sure it’s as fun and polished as possible!
 
[b]Emiel De Paepe [/b]

Emiel has been knee-deep in the arts from an early age, picking up drawing and painting as a kid. At 15, he discovered Photoshop, which set him on a path that eventually led to game development in 2011. That’s where he found the perfect outlet for both his creative and technical skills. Now, he’s using that artistic flair and technical know-how to help shape the colorful world of Nubs!

[b]Jeroen van Wamelen [/b]

Jeroen kicked off his career as a modder back in 1998, turning his passion into a profession by 2009. Specializing in art and level design, he also builds tools to make these processes smoother. Jeroen’s mission? To craft games oozing with atmosphere, and he’s bringing that same vibe to Nubs! with immersive levels and creative design!

[b]Betül Bacak [/b]

Betül graduated cum laude from Howest DAE and honed her skills as an animator and illustrator at Vlaams Steunpunt VZW while still studying. She even worked as an artist on the animated film Dikkie Dik. With drawing and painting as second nature to her, Betül’s true passion is crafting concept art for both games and animated films, bringing her artistic vision to life in Nubs! with style and creativity.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227533/62bafbe19e3fb0ee9b406623cc8eb39215027579.png[/img]
That’s a wrap for our very first Nublog! Now you’ve met the talented crew from Rangatang and Glowfish, the creative forces behind Nubs! Each of these amazing devs is bringing their unique skills and passions to make Nubs! a ridiculously fun, chaotic, and unforgettable experience. We can’t wait to share more as we continue shaping the world of Nubs!

Stay tuned for future Nublogs, as from now on content and development updates will be shared with you every two weeks. Get ready to unleash your inner Nub!
-Greetings, Nublognub

notes.title: Announcing Nubs! The Chaos Fuelled Arena Brawler!
notes.content:
Welcome fellow Nub, good to see you made it! I’m afraid there’s no time for formalities, Konzumos the Unentertained demands to be amused! 

Nubs! is an absurd PvP arena brawler game inspired by old-school, top-down RPG’s. Guide your Nub through a variety of treacherous arenas brimming with traps. Find ridiculous weapons to use on your friends and choose new power-ups after every round. All to become Konzumos’ favorite. 

[previewyoutube=gJb-2T4_rrw;full][/previewyoutube]

The core design of Nubs! was adapted by former members of the now closed studio Ronimo Games – and refined together with Glowfish Interactive. When the game launches in 2025, players can expect an enjoyably chaotic modern multiplayer experience with the charm and nostalgia of classic indie games.

We at Rangatang and Glowfish hope that you like what you see, and if so, be sure to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2337860/Nubs/]wishlist Nubs! on Steam[/url] to get notified on great milestones. Interested in more about Nubs!? Follow our [url=https://x.com/FollowNubs]X[/url] or [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/nubs/]Nubreddit[/url] for weekly posts and news on the game.

We would love to hear what you think and if you’re interested, in the future we’ll be looking for people to playtest with, so be sure to [url=https://discord.com/invite/nubs]join our Discord community[/url] to talk to us and fellow Nubs! 



All hail Konzumos,
-The Nubs!
